newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Outsiders blamed for Indonesian ethnic violence.
newsitem.headline: Outsiders blamed for Indonesian ethnic violence.

text.p: Indonesia's army chief has blamed outsiders from East Java for outbreaks of ethnic violence in West Kalimantan province on Borneo island, the official Antara news agency reported on Monday.
"We have proof, there were bad people from East Java who came there to incite, so something happened which we did not want," General Hartono told reporters at army headquarters in Jakarta on Monday.
He said West Kalimantan, which borders Malaysia's Sarawak state, was peaceful before the arrival of the outsiders from East Java.
"The people were harmonious. After the bad people came, they were restless again," he said, without giving further details.

Ethnic riots broke out in West Kalimantan in late December in what police said was a fight between Dayak and Maduran youths over a girl at a concert in Sanggau Ledo, about 95 km (60 miles) north of Pontianak, the provincial capital.
The fighting between ethnic Dayaks and Madurans, who are migrants from Madura island off East Java, later spread to other parts of West Kalimantan.
The military and residents in the province say at least 12 people have died over the past six weeks. Some residents and church sources say the figure could be much higher.
Residents say troops still guard several towns even though calm has gradually returned to the province.
Officials said traditional ceremonies to ease tension had been held in the interior between the Dayaks and Madurans.
Most Dayaks are Christians while Maduran migrants are Moslems.
At least 19 people have died in religious and ethnic riots in mainly Moslem Indonesia since October.
